theme: The hidden cost of a bad venue choice — real production numbers

linkedin.text:
We got a call 11 days before a 400-person leadership summit.

The venue was already signed. The problem: wrong ceiling clearance, no load-in dock, AV dead zones throughout the main hall.

Here's what that actually cost the client:
+22% on logistics
+14 hours of replanning
1 near-miss on stage rigging

We delivered. The event ran flawlessly. But the budget hit was real.

After 16 years and 1,500+ events across 130+ destinations, the single most expensive mistake we see senior HR and marketing leaders make is treating venue selection as a hospitality decision instead of a production infrastructure decision.

The room you book determines what experience is physically possible. Full stop.

If you're in planning mode right now — DM me before you sign. Happy to do a 15-minute brief review, no strings attached.

What's the toughest venue constraint you've ever had to engineer around? I'm curious.

facebook.text:
We once received a brief 11 days before a 400-person leadership summit.

The client had already locked a venue — wrong ceiling height, no loading dock, AV blackout zones in every corner.

We didn't panic. We renegotiated, re-routed the production flow, and delivered on time.

But it added 22% to the logistics budget — money that should have gone into the experience.

After 1,500+ events in 130+ destinations, here's the one thing we tell every HR and marketing lead before they sign a venue contract:

👉 Your venue is not a backdrop. It's infrastructure.
